GARVIDA Municipal Mayor Municipality of Nueva Era Ilocos Norte Dear Mayor Garvida: s. 2012 This is in reference to your letter dated 15 November 2017 submitting to this Department the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Resolution No. 2017-88, with this prayer: "WHEREFORE, be it enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan of Nueva Era, Ilocos Norte, that: RESOLVED, AS IT HEREBY RESOLVED, TO EARNESTLY REQUEST HON CATALINO S coy, SECRETARY, DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT, TO ORDER THE' REGIONAL DIRECTOR AND PROVINCIAL DIRECTOR TO IMPLEMENT THE SANGGUNIANG PAIVL4L4 WIGAN ORDER ON BOUNDARY DISPUTE 104 COGNIZANT TO SUPREME COURT EN BANC DECISION UNDER G.R. 169435 RE: TRANSFER OF POLITICAL JURISDICTION FROM BRGY. CACAFEAN AND PARTS OF BARANGAY FERDINAND AND ELIZABETH, MARCOS TO THE POLITICAL JURISDICTION OFIVUEVA ERA, ILOCOS NORTE. RESOLVED FINALLY, to furnish copies of this resolution to HON. CA TALINO S. GUY, for his information and favorable action. " Per evaluation of the SB Resolution shows that your Municipality is requesting this Department to implement the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Order on Boundary Dispute 104 as the same was affirmed by the Supreme Court En Banc in its Decision in G.R. No. 169435. Please be informed that this issue has long been settled in DILG Opinion No. 37, s. 2008, the salient provision is quoted hereunder:

"Article 17 (h) of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides in full: "(h) Decision — Within sixty (60) days from the date the certification was issued, the dispute shall be formally tried and decided by the sanggunian concerned. Copies of the decision shall, within fifteen (15) days from the promulgation thereof, be furnished the parties concerned, DILG local assessor, Comelec, NSO, and other NGAs concerned. " Parenthetically, Article 19 of the same Implementing Rules and Regulations provides: "ART. 19. Official Custodian. - The DILG shall be the official custodian of copies of all documents on boundary disputes of LGUs. " It is. therefore. evident from the aforequotedprovisions that the DILG's role in decisions rendered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigal? pertaining to ounda dis utes would onl be that of an official cust Ian of d umen relative to the dispute. Nowhere in the Local Government Code of 1991 or its Implementing Rules and Regulations mandate the Department to ainin to bounda dis utes. Along this line, you are hereby advised to inform the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Vizcaya of the Department's role on the matter as aforestated and to further inform the said Sanggunian that in implementing its decision, Article 17 (h) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code requires them to immediately furnish the parties concerned copy of the decision. The parties concerned are immediately furnished copy of the decision so that they may, within the prescriptive period, still exercise available legal remedies, such as an appeal before the Regional Trial Court having jurisdiction over the area in dispute as provided for in Section 119 of the Local Government Code. " In view of the foregoing, we regret to inform you that this Department has no power under the Local Government Code (LGC) and other laws to implement the decisions on boundary disputes between local government units (LGUs). However, in line with the Department's supervisory function over LGUs, your Municipality, the Municipality of Marcos and the Province of Ilocos Norte are hereby advised to comply with Section 118 (d) and (e) of

the LGC, Rule III of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGC and with the Decision dated 27 February 2008 of the Supreme Court. Lastly, rest assured that we will inform DILG Regional Director and Provincial Director regarding the said Decision. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Reading of the Supreme Court Decision shows that it granted the Nueva Era's petition, and reversed the CA Decision, the Highest Court said: "Only Dingras is specifically named by law as source territory of Marcos. Hence, the said description of boundaries of Marcos is descriptive only of the listed barangays of Dingras as a compact and contagious territory.. Considering that the description of the eastern boundary of Marcos under R.A. No. 3753 is ambiguous, the same must be interpreted in light OT the legislative intent. The law must be given a reasonable interpretation, to preclude absurdity in its application. We thus uphold the legislative intent to create Marcos out OT the territory of Dingras only. Moreover, the Supreme Court reinstated the RTC Ilocos Norte Decision which affirmed the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Decision dated 29 March 2000, the dispositive portion of which, provides: "WHEREFORE, in view of the foregoing, this Body has no alternative but to dismiss, as it hereby DISMISSES said petition for lack of merit. The disputed area consisting of 15, 400 hectares, more or less, is hereby declared as part and portion of the territorial jurisdiction of respondent Nueva Era. SO ORDERED.
